head: Signal
Answers
Tools
rows: Is something wrong? (rates, errors, latency, saturation)
What exactly happened in this request?
Where did the time go across services?

items: **RED** for services: Rate, Errors, Duration. **USE** for resources: Utilisation, Saturation, Errors.
Structured (JSON) logs with a request/trace id on every line.
Percentiles (p50/p95/p99), not averages — averages hide the slow tail users feel.

blocks.caption: One trace id follows the request

blocks.text: Each service creates a span with timing and attributes and propagates the trace context in headers (W3C traceparent). Sampling (e.g. keep 1% plus all errors and slow requests) keeps costs manageable.

items: **SLI:** a measured indicator, e.g. % of requests under 300 ms and non-5xx.
**SLO:** the target, e.g. 99.9% over 30 days → an **error budget** of 0.1% (~43 minutes).
Alert on **burn rate** of the error budget (fast burn pages someone; slow burn opens a ticket) rather than on every CPU spike.
Every alert should be actionable and link to a runbook.

cols.title: JWT access tokens
cons: Hard to revoke before expiry — keep them short-lived (5–15 min) with refresh tokens

items: **OAuth 2.0 / OIDC** for delegated access and SSO; PKCE for mobile/SPA clients.
Authorise every request on the server (RBAC/ABAC); never trust client-side checks.
Service-to-service identity via mTLS (service mesh) or signed workload tokens.

sections.title: Security checklist interviewers like to hear

head: Area
Practice
rows: TLS everywhere; HSTS; mTLS internally where possible
Encryption with KMS-managed keys; per-tenant keys for sensitive data
Secret manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager), never in code or images
Validate and parameterise queries (SQL injection), encode output (XSS), CSRF tokens
Rate limiting, WAF, bot detection, CAPTCHAs on sensitive endpoints
Scoped IAM roles per service; short-lived credentials
Immutable audit logs for admin and data access
Minimise, tokenise, set retention; support deletion requests

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: I'd instrument every service with OpenTelemetry for traces and RED metrics, alert on SLO burn rate, use short-lived JWTs issued by an OIDC provider, mTLS between services, and keep secrets in a managed vault.

items: Canary or blue/green releases with automated rollback on SLO regression.
Feature flags to decouple deploy from release and to kill features quickly.
